hook.line: Tomás was late opening the café again, and everyone wants the story. Most of the verbs he needs for it change their stem in the past, but they all share one set of endings.
hook.es: Tuve que salir y no pude abrir a las siete.
hook.en: I had to go out and I couldn't open at seven.

examples.es: Estuvimos dos horas en el trancón.
examples.en: We were stuck in traffic for two hours.
Where were you last night? (to a friend)

examples.es: Mi abuela me dio una foto.
examples.en: My grandmother gave me a photo.

rule:
A group of everyday verbs gets a new stem in the past:
*tener*: *tuv-*
*estar*: *estuv-*
*poder*: *pud-*
*poner*: *pus-*
*venir*: *vin-*
*querer*: *quis-*
*decir*: *dij-*
*traer*: *traj-*

Then they all take the same endings: *-e*, *-iste*, *-o*, *-imos*, *-ieron*. So *tuve*, *tuviste*, *tuvo*, *tuvimos*, *tuvieron*.

Two things look odd. There are no accent marks: it's *tuve* and *pudo*, not *tuvé* or *pudó*. And after a *j*, they lose the *i*: *dijeron*, *trajeron*.

*Dar* and *ver* are short and plain: *di*, *dio*, *dimos*, *dieron*; *vi*, *vio*, *vimos*, *vieron*. Also no accents.

*No pude* is more than I couldn't: it means I tried and it didn't happen.
smallPrint: Teachers call these the strong (or irregular) preterites: the stress falls on the stem in *tuve* and *tuvo*, not on the ending.
soundTip: Say *tuve* as TOO-beh and *tuvo* as TOO-boh, stress on the first syllable. Compare regular *compré* and *compró*, stressed at the end. That missing accent mark is a stress you don't put there.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap and type the whole sentence: *Ayer ___ que trabajar.* (*tuve* or *tuvo*) I had to work yesterday.
yourTurn.why: I had is *tuve*; *tuvo* is he or she.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap and type the whole sentence: *Vale ___ pan.* (*traje* or *trajo*) Vale brought bread.
yourTurn.why: Vale is she, so *trajo*; *traje* is I brought.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Where were you last night?
yourTurn.why: To a friend, you were is *estuviste*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about we: *Tuve un problema.*
Make it negative: *Estuvo en el café.*
Ask Don Hernando, politely: Did you bring the photo?
yourTurn.why: With *usted*, it's the he and she form: *trajo*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Tener* changes its stem in the past: *tuve*.
Close. These forms have no accent mark, and the stress sits on the stem: *pude*.
Nearly. After the *j* the *i* drops out: *dijeron*.

personal: Tell the story of a bad day. Write three sentences with *tuve que*, *no pude* and one more from the list (*vine*, *estuve*, *traje*, *dije*).
